arm_dials.row_weighting: 1/near_dup_group_size on the TRAIN side; the eval side keeps one row per group (data/render_mode_corpus/near_dup_groups_v1.json)

candidate_selection: max eval AP>=2 (marginal P>=2, 'not bad') on the deduplicated pooled eval side; full schedule, no early stop — v1's OWN objective, the (28b) fifth arm
moves_nothing: no pin, gate, floor, lock or annotation is written by this file

eval_slice.deduplicated: one row per near-dup group (colored-CLIP, cut 0.974)

split.rule: union-find over locations linked by Julia-seed == parent-plane point; family-stratified seeded draw over UNITS, not locations
split.disjointness: 293 units, each wholly on one side

near_dup.substrate: colored_clip — palette-ON CLIP vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai, timm eval transform (tools/curation/colored_clip.py)

harness_parity.what: v1 re-scored here vs the head_mining_v1.p_ge3 stamped into images.jsonl at sheet-build time. Same checkpoint, same deploy transform, days apart.

v1_unseen_locations.what: eval rows at locations the v1 sitting never served — v1 has not memorised these and their labels were not anchored to a v1 suggestion at a location it had already judged. The only cell where the two v1-inflating caveats are off.

v3_seed_band.note: each seed's own best-epoch checkpoint, every one of them selected on THIS eval side; the band is over seeds, not over held-out populations, and the staged max is optimistic against it.

score_scale.why: a fixed threshold is a point on ONE head's scale; the live cuts are NOT restated here, and a flip would have to volume-match them (classifier_retrain_protocol.md §5a).

winner_rule.rule: v3 wins iff (a) no pre-declared no-worse arm is significantly worse than v1 (95% paired-bootstrap CI on the delta not entirely below 0) AND (b) on the motivating arm at least one metric is significantly better and none is significantly worse. Otherwise v1 keeps candidacy.
winner_rule.multiplicity_note: clause (a) is a conjunction over 38 arm x metric cells; at 95% per cell the chance one crosses by luck alone is material, so read `failures` before reading `pass`.
winner_rule.adoption: NOT decided here. BUILD != FLIP: adoption is a separate prompt after Matt reads this verdict.
